squash_access@2006.rationale: Registered-player intensity remains the strongest organised-access proxy in the current canonical evidence, with club footprint as a secondary structural-access proxy. Source definitions vary by association, so this remains provisional evidence rather than a final access rating.

competition_quality@2023.rationale: Professional ecosystem scale is primary because domestic competition quality depends on having substantial absolute player and club depth; per-capita density is retained only as a secondary saturation signal. Counts still do not directly measure league quality or results.

elite_support@2023.rationale: Elite-support evidence is anchored primarily in the absolute professional club and employment ecosystem, with density retained as secondary evidence of institutional saturation. Funding, medical/science provision and federation technical quality remain unmeasured.

unsupported_attributes.squash_popularity: Participation intensity alone materially underestimates football cultural popularity in multiple review countries (notably Japan, India, Morocco and Senegal) and overstates the USA; canonical popularity needs independent cultural/audience evidence.
unsupported_attributes.development_quality: No canonical normalized source in the current slice directly measures coaching, academies, talent identification or youth pathway quality.
unsupported_attributes.squash_tradition: A 2006/2023 cross-sectional signal cannot measure long-term institutional/cultural continuity.

safeguards: Evidence score is not a canonical country rating.
Popularity has no quantitative 1–10 recipe until independent cultural/audience evidence is normalized.
Professional ecosystem scale and density are separate signals; density alone must never be treated as competition quality or elite support.
No recipe may use a signal outside its declared primary dimensions without an explicit model revision.
Missing required components produce a missing evidence score; missing is never zero.
Scores are rounded to one decimal only after component weighting.
No score is extrapolated beyond the declared percentile transfer curve.
A future canonical rating must combine quantitative evidence with independent historical/context evidence and explicit observation provenance.
